0.title: Course Introduction
0.content:
The Loire Valley is famous for its whites, but its reds and rosés are just as exciting — and surprise many people. Cabernet Franc reaches its world peak in Chinon and Bourgueil, Gamay offers fresh fruit, Côt (Malbec) brings structure, and Pineau d'Aunis wins over natural-wine lovers with its peppery character.

Learning Objectives

🍇 Master Cabernet Franc's special expression in the Loire

Understand why the cool Loire climate lets Cabernet Franc show a refined style completely different from Bordeaux

🫐 Know the roles of Gamay and Côt

Each has its stage in Touraine, offering choices from fresh to structured

🌶️ Understand the unique character of Pineau d'Aunis

This native variety, found almost only in the Loire Valley, has become a natural-wine favourite for its spicy character
1.title: Cabernet Franc: King of Loire Reds
1.highlights.0.title: Elegance and refinement in fresh red fruit
1.highlights.0.content: In the cool Loire climate, Cabernet Franc shows mainly red fruit (raspberry, redcurrant), florals (violet) and minerality, with fine tannins
1.highlights.1.title: The vegetal misconception
1.highlights.1.content: A slight green-grass / green-pepper aroma is a varietal characteristic of Cabernet Franc and almost disappears in very ripe vintages; only underripe grapes taste harsh
1.content:
In Bordeaux Cabernet Franc plays a supporting role (a blending partner for Merlot), but in the Loire Valley it is the undisputed star. The cool climate and tuffeau and gravel soils let Cabernet Franc show the most refined and aromatic face in the world.

🍇 Varietal character

Colour

Medium ruby to garnet, rarely deep black tones

Aroma

Raspberry, redcurrant, violet, green grass / green pepper (when young), spice, leaf mould (with age)

Tannin

Fine and silky, much softer than Bordeaux's Cabernet Sauvignon

Acidity

High, a guarantee of ageing potential

Style differences

Gravel sites: fresh fruit, for early drinking
Tuffeau sites: stronger structure, can age 10–20 years

🏅 Core Cabernet Franc AOPs

Chinon

Location: Vienne valley, southwest of Tours
Soils: tuffeau uplands (complex, age-worthy wines) + gravel plain (fresh, early-drinking wines)
Style: the widest stylistic range, from light fruity to complex aged wines; well-known producers: Olga Raffault, Bernard Baudry, Philippe Alliet

Bourgueil

Location: right bank of the Loire
Soils: tuffeau hills + gravelly sand
Style: more minerality and structure than Chinon, with aged wines showing humus and leather; well-known producers: Yannick Amirault, Catherine et Pierre Breton

Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil

Location: west of Bourgueil
Soils: mainly sand and gravel, with a little tuffeau
Style: the lightest and freshest of the three; bright raspberry fruit, suited to serving slightly cool, for early drinking

Saumur-Champigny

Location: south of Saumur
Soils: tuffeau
Style: silky and round, dominated by red fruit (raspberry, strawberry), with tuffeau giving a distinctive minerality; the Loire's most popular red AOP
1.quiz.question: What is the main stylistic difference between Cabernet Franc from the Loire Valley and from Bordeaux?
1.quiz.options.0: The Loire's is richer, with more black fruit and chocolate
1.quiz.options.1: The Loire's is fresher and more refined, mainly red fruit and minerality, with fine tannins
1.quiz.explanation: In the cool Loire climate, Cabernet Franc retains more natural acidity, with fresh red fruit (raspberry, redcurrant) and fine, elegant tannins. Bordeaux, by contrast, is warmer; there Cabernet Franc provides aroma and acidity in blends, but combined with Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon the overall style is heavier. Chinon and Bourgueil in the Loire are the highest temples of Cabernet Franc as a single variety.
2.title: Gamay and Côt (Malbec)
2.highlights.0.title: Gamay: the voice of fresh fruit
2.highlights.0.content: Widely planted in Touraine for light, refreshing everyday reds; also often blended with Cabernet Franc or Côt
2.highlights.1.title: Côt = Malbec: dark structure in the Loire
2.highlights.1.content: Touraine-Amboise is the only legally defined AOP that makes red wine from 100% Côt; it brings depth of colour, fruit concentration and structure
2.content:
🍓 Gamay

Main areas: Touraine, Coteaux d'Ancenis, Anjou

Loire character: similar to Beaujolais Gamay, but Loire versions usually do not use carbonic maceration (macération carbonique), so the style differs slightly — more sense of soil, less of a fruit-candy style

Aroma: redcurrant, strawberry, violet, a hint of pepper

Tannin: light and smooth, low astringency

Uses:

  • Basic Touraine red (single variety)
  • Blended with Côt: Touraine Gamay-Côt (adds colour and structure)
  • Blended with Cabernet Franc: adds fruit and freshness

Serving temperature: 12–14°C (served slightly chilled to highlight fresh fruit)

🫐 Côt (= Malbec)

Name in the Loire: usually called "Côt" (sometimes also Malbec or Auxerrois)

Main areas: Touraine, Touraine-Amboise, Touraine-Chenonceaux

Special status: Touraine-Amboise is the only legally defined AOP that makes red wine from 100% Côt, which is very rare in the world (Argentine Malbec is almost always blended with other varieties)

Aroma: black plum, blueberry, cocoa, liquorice, violet

Style: deep colour, more tannin, medium to fairly full body; more acidity and finesse than Argentine Malbec

Blending role: in Anjou reds it often plays a supporting role to Cabernet Franc or Cabernet Sauvignon, adding colour and fruit concentration
2.quiz.question: Which Loire Valley AOP is the only appellation in the world that requires red wine to be made from 100% Côt (Malbec)?
2.quiz.explanation: Touraine-Amboise is the only AOP in the Loire Valley (indeed in France) that explicitly requires red wine to be made from 100% Côt (that is, Malbec). Côt is planted elsewhere in the Loire, but usually as a blending variety; only Touraine-Amboise makes it the single-variety star. Compared with its fame in Argentina, this makes it understated and special.
3.title: Pineau d'Aunis: A Spicy Native
3.highlights.0.title: The strange aroma of pepper and wildflowers
3.highlights.0.content: Pineau d'Aunis is almost exclusive to the Loire, known for its distinctive white pepper, red fruit and wildflower aromas, and is much sought after in the natural-wine world
3.highlights.1.title: A revival after near extinction
3.highlights.1.content: Almost entirely uprooted in the mid-20th century, it is now regaining attention thanks to natural winemakers; the Vendômois and Coteaux du Loir are the main strongholds
3.content:
Pineau d'Aunis is the Loire Valley's most distinctive native red grape, grown almost exclusively in the Loire Valley (mainly around the Loir and Vendôme). Once considered old-fashioned and close to disappearing, it has been driven by the natural-wine movement to become one of today's most talked-about "rare varieties."

🍇 Varietal character

  • Colour: pale, ruby to garnet, with strong transparency
  • Aroma: white pepper (very typical!), redcurrant, rose petals, wild strawberry, stony minerality
  • Acidity: high, with a lively palate
  • Tannin: light to medium, light texture
  • Alcohol: naturally lowish, suited to everyday drinking

📍 Main areas

Coteaux du Vendômois

The most important stronghold of Pineau d'Aunis, where many producers make red and rosé from 100% Pineau d'Aunis; locally "Pineau d'Aunis en rosé" is almost the most prized style

Coteaux du Loir

The Loir valley (note: "Loir", not "Loire" — a northern tributary), with a cool climate that makes Pineau d'Aunis' spiciness stand out more

Jasnières

Though famous for Chenin Blanc whites, there is also a little Pineau d'Aunis red; very rare, a collectors' treasure

🌱 Darling of the natural-wine world

Thanks to its naturally low acidity, low alcohol and distinctive spicy character, Pineau d'Aunis has become a favourite of natural-wine (vin naturel) producers. Its "not-too-much" nature — not deep, not sweet, not heavy — has made it popular in a contemporary drinking culture that seeks lightness and freshness.
3.quiz.question: What is the most distinctive aroma of Pineau d'Aunis?
3.quiz.options.1: White pepper spice with red fruit and floral notes
3.quiz.explanation: Pineau d'Aunis is known for its distinctive white-pepper spiciness, very rare among red grape varieties (pepper notes are more often the black pepper of Syrah than the white pepper of Pineau d'Aunis). Together with the fresh fruit of redcurrant, rose petals and wild strawberry, it forms this variety's unique aromatic profile.
4.title: Red Grape Quick Reference and Food Pairing
4.highlights.0.title: The philosophy of light reds
4.highlights.0.content: Loire reds are generally fresh and light rather than concentrated and heavy, so they suit a wide range of foods and can be served slightly cool
4.highlights.1.title: Better slightly chilled
4.highlights.1.content: Many Loire reds (especially Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil and Gamay) are served at 14–16°C, slightly cooler than typical reds, to bring out the fruit
4.content:
📊 Quick comparison of Loire Valley red grapes

Variety Representative AOPs Core style Ideal serving temperature
Cabernet Franc Chinon, Bourgueil, Saumur-Champigny Red fruit, minerality, fine tannins 14–17°C
Gamay Touraine, Coteaux d'Ancenis Fresh fruit, light and easy-drinking 12–14°C
Côt (Malbec) Touraine-Amboise, Touraine Dark fruit, more structure 15–17°C
Pineau d'Aunis Vendômois, Coteaux du Loir Peppery spice, light and transparent 12–14°C
Pinot Noir Sancerre, Menetou-Salon Refined and elegant, red fruit and florals 14–16°C

🍽️ Red wine food pairing guide

Chinon / Bourgueil (old-vine tuffeau wines)

Wild boar stew, duck dishes, aged goat cheese, sausages

Saumur-Champigny

Grilled salmon, duck breast, lightly roasted lamb chops, mushroom dishes

Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil

Roast chicken, duck leg confit, vegetable dishes, mild cheeses

Gamay / Pineau d'Aunis

Light cold dishes, charcuterie, country picnics, vegetarian dishes
4.quiz.question: Why are many Loire reds (such as Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil) recommended to be served slightly cooler (14–16°C) than typical reds?
4.quiz.options.0: Because these wines contain a lot of residual sugar, and cool temperatures highlight sweetness
4.quiz.options.1: Cool serving makes the fresh fruit and acidity stand out, which suits the Loire's light, fresh style
4.quiz.options.2: These wines cannot tolerate room temperature and would oxidise
4.quiz.options.3: Chilled red is a Loire tradition
4.quiz.explanation: Light Loire reds (such as Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil and Gamay de Touraine) served at slightly lower temperatures bring out fresh red-fruit aromas (raspberry, strawberry) while keeping the lively palate from naturally high acidity. If served too warm (say 20°C), alcohol becomes more prominent and the delicate fruit is masked, losing the light freshness that makes these wines so charming.
